findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process ... executed with Tool-level rigor” names the rubric patterns without helping the agent configure lanes; Step 0 already shows the sequence.
findings.fix: Keep the instruction to use the factory subcommands and the reason guessed IDs or malformed fields fail late. Record the removal of the rubric labels; keep the Evidence section intact.

findings.evidence: “### Step 1 — Detect” through “### Step 4 — Report” are nested under “## NEVER,” while Step 0 is nested under “## Your task.” The document hierarchy splits the otherwise clear operational sequence.
findings.fix: Make Steps 0–4 peer headings with unchanged titles, and nest each numbered substep under its parent. Keep the NEVER list separate from the procedure.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” gives a clear setup trigger, but does not name stale OpenCode provider checks, explain the migrate-only behavior, or distinguish setup from running configured lanes. “--check-only (report availability, no writes)” also omits the possibility of a consented live probe.
findings.fix: Use when the user wants to set up or refresh ai-kit’s cross-AI review or execution lanes, choose which installed CLIs and models to use and in what order, check availability or stale OpenCode providers, or ask about migrating review-spec.toml. Detects runtimes, proposes separate review and execute sets, and saves owner-confirmed orders, effort and opt-in settings in config.toml. Announces the target: .aikit/config.toml by default or with --local, the user ai-kit/config.toml with --global. Always asks before replacing an existing roster. --check-only leaves config and persistent caches unchanged; live probes with unconfirmed write permissions require consent. For migration alone, report the pending migration rather than starting setup. Not for running configured lanes or editing unrelated tables.

findings.evidence: “codex’s model field must be the BARE model id” starts a long inline runtime-specific block, although Step 2.4 already gates runtime profiles by selection. The 425-line entrypoint is about 40 KB and loads this detail even for runs that stop before lane selection.
findings.fix: Keep the pair-versus-custom decision and the selected-profile trigger inline. Move the detailed Codex listing and Cursor ID-construction instructions and examples to their selected-runtime profiles or a focused Step 2.4 reference, preserving the bare-ID and separate-effort rules.

findings.evidence: “Loaded from wizard-flow.md step 2 only” conflicts with the explicit Step 6 load for item 6, so an agent taking the ordinary matched-candidate branch gets contradictory loading instructions.
findings.fix: State both gates in the reference: load items 1–4 for a missing listing or unmatched candidates, and use item 6 at the kept-lane code-index check. Keep the other instructions at their existing workflow steps.

findings.evidence: The two adjacent “catalog-report” commands offer live detection and cached inventory without selecting one as the default. The distinction matters because only a successful live listing can substantiate a stale row.
findings.fix: Use --detect for ordinary interactive setup. Use --runtimes-json only when live detection is unavailable or the owner asks to rely on the saved snapshot, and preserve the resulting “not checked” label.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” can pass when no alias is shown. The roster fixture alone does not supply a live listing or catalog row that forces that branch.
findings.fix: Supply a deterministic listing or catalog fixture that includes the router alias. Assert that the alias appears in the separate unranked group with its assumed label and that the wizard asks no heuristic question about it.

findings.evidence: The suite has 10 positives and 10 negatives, but negatives such as “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill” test little, and the only positive about execute-lane selection is bundled with review selection.
findings.fix: Replace the unrelated negatives with near-misses such as troubleshooting a failed configured execute lane. Replace one redundant review-setup positive with an execute-only setup request that mentions neither the wizard nor cross-AI.

findings.evidence: “Run the catalog flow” comes before Step 2.1’s replacement consent. With an installed runtime lacking a listing, fetch-model-catalog calls cfg_resolve with migration enabled (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/ai_kit_spec/cli.py:572–580), so a pending roster can be migrated and the old file retired before the owner chooses Stop or Keep Backup.
findings.fix: Make catalog discovery read existing and pending rosters without migration. Keep migration and retirement behind the write target’s explicit replacement and backup decision; verify that Stop leaves both roster layers untouched.

findings.evidence: “write one correction only with confirm-model” is prescribed for an unmatched candidate absent from the catalog. That command rejects an absent key as “unknown catalog key” (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/ai_kit_spec/catalog_cmds.py:64–69).
findings.fix: After owner confirmation, use confirm-catalog-entry with validated entry JSON for a genuinely new key, preserving any runtime-reported effort metadata. Use confirm-model only to amend a key that already exists. Check the result before proposing the candidate.

findings.evidence: “Run Step 2.5’s write-risk question and test call for every chosen table-runtime lane” leaves out the documented custom-command route. A kept Grok or custom-script lane can reach the write without the promised test or a recorded decision to skip it.
findings.fix: Route custom lanes through the same test-or-explicit-skip gate. Treat an arbitrary custom command as having unconfirmed write permissions, show its template before asking, and use check-reviewer --command only after consent. Carry the custom lane’s source CLI separately for the advisory code-index check.

findings.evidence: “--show writes no trust record” is not true for every path: trust-local calls cfg_migrate_project before branching on --show, and migration can carry an old trust record into the new store. The merged preview can also migrate the user roster (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/ai_kit_spec/cli.py:1113–1153).
findings.fix: Make --show resolve both layers without migration or trust writes, and document that guarantee only once it holds. Keep the explicit owner consent gate for the trusting form.

findings.evidence: “the runner refuses a model id its runtime’s grammar disallows” contradicts the referenced runner contract: skills/ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md:47 says an unusual ID shape produces an advisory and still runs.
findings.fix: Distinguish a non-blocking runner shape advisory from a routing inventory rejection or a live CLI rejection. Keep the live pair test as the check for whether the selected ID actually works.

findings.evidence: “the table in ai-kit-spec.py’s _MODEL_VENDOR_PREFIXES” points to a symbol the launcher does not define; it lives in skills/ai-kit-spec-review/ai_kit_spec/vendor.py:20. The table is a best-effort prefix lookup, not proof of complete model-family coverage.
findings.fix: Point to vendor.py if the implementation location is useful, describe the lookup as best effort, and retain the instruction to ask the owner when infer-vendor returns null.

findings.evidence: “If any entries exist” conditions the merged preflight on the preceding raw target read. With no local file but an inherited global roster, that raw read finds nothing even though probe-quota can spawn for global lanes.
findings.fix: Run the read-only merged preflight regardless of whether the selected raw file contains lanes. Use the merged probe keys to decide whether to ask about risk or probe at all, and keep the raw listing only for explaining which layer supplied each result.
